## **11\. Lab-Report and Viva Preparation**

### **11.1 Suggested Lab-Report Outline and Essential Figures/Tables**

**\[Engineering Recommendation\]** The final written course report should be formatted as an 8-to-10-page IEEE two-column manuscript structured into seven sections. **Section 1 (Abstract & Introduction)** frames the problem of text-independent speaker verification, the limitations of fixed-kernel 1D TDNNs and clean-label assumptions, and the scope of our scaled reproduction on LibriSpeech1. **Section 2 (Mathematical Formulation of SKA-HNN and IAAMSoftmax)** presents the exact equations for fwSKA versus cwSKA9, sliding-window Local Statistics, MLFC \+ MLASP, and IAAMSoftmax (AdaptiveDrop label correction and cosine filtering)1, explicitly highlighting our correction of Equation (3)'s denominator index (![][image243])1 and incorporating **Table 1 (Full vs. Scaled Tensor-Shape and Parameter Audit)**. **Section 3 (Experimental Protocol & Dataset Engineering)** justifies selecting 16 kHz LibriSpeech (train-clean-100, dev-clean, test-clean, test-other) over 24 kHz LibriTTS14, details the cross-chapter target and gender-matched impostor trial generation algorithm, and explains the hardware-aware channel scaling (![][image444] parameters).  
**Section 4 (Supervised Verification Results & Ablation Study)** presents **Table 2 (Master Baseline and Ablation Table across ![][image445] and ![][image24] with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals)**, **Figure 1 (DET Curves and Target vs. Impostor Cosine Score Histograms on test-clean and test-other)**, and **Figure 2 (Short-Utterance Robustness Curve at ![][image414], and Full Duration)**. **Section 5 (Label-Noise Robustness & Self-Supervised Clustering Evaluation)** presents **Table 3 (AAMSoftmax vs. IAAMSoftmax across ![][image334] synthetic label noise and ![][image335] K-Means pseudo-labels)** alongside **Figure 3 (Validation EER and AdaptiveDrop Retention Rate vs. Epoch under ![][image336] and ![][image337] label noise)**, demonstrating visually how IAAMSoftmax prevents noisy-label memorization after Epoch 53. **Section 6 (Explainability & Interactive System Demonstration)** includes **Figure 4 (fwSKA frequency-band attention heatmap across the 40 Mel bins, MLASP frame-level attention weights over an utterance spectrogram, and a 2D UMAP projection of 20 test speakers)**. Finally, **Section 7 (Limitations & Conclusion)** synthesizes the findings and discusses speaker-count scaling laws20, audiobook-to-wild domain mismatch, and parameter compression of the TDNN-LSTM transition layer.

### **11.2 Fifteen Likely Examiner Questions with Model Technical Answers**

| \# | Likely Examiner Viva Question | Concise, High-Authority Technical Answer |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Q1** | Why does SKA-HNN apply Selective Kernel Attention along *both* the frequency axis (fwSKA) and the channel axis (cwSKA) inside the 2D-CNN front-end? | In a 2D spectrogram (![][image446]), channels represent distinct local spectro-temporal filters, whereas frequency bins correspond to physical vocal-tract resonances (![][image59] pitch and ![][image447]–![][image448] formants)8. Standard cwSKA pools across ![][image50], collapsing frequency-specific scale differences8. Applying fwSKA first (pooling across ![][image61] to yield an ![][image449]\-dim vector) lets the network select a ![][image40] kernel in narrow low-frequency pitch bands and a ![][image41] kernel in broader high-frequency formant transitions before cwSKA recalibrates channel importance1. |
| **Q2** | Why does the paper cascade a TDNN-LSTM module and a Fully-TDNN module after the 2D-CNN, and why is MLFC (![][image345]) necessary? | The three modules contribute complementary inductive biases: the 2D-CNN (![][image80]) captures fine local time-frequency patterns, the TDNN-LSTM (![][image81]) models long-range sequential/prosodic trajectories, and the dilated Fully-TDNN (![][image223]) captures medium-range multi-scale phoneme transitions1. Because recurrent LSTMs can compress fine spectral details, MLFC creates a direct residual highway from all three levels into MLASP, explaining why removing MLFC (![][image450]) degrades EER by ![][image451] relative (![][image12])1. |
| **Q3** | How does Local Statistics (LS) pooling differ from the final Attentive Statistics Pooling (ASP), and why is it appended to ![][image82] inside MLASP? | Final ASP collapses the entire time axis ![][image86] into a single utterance vector (![][image452])1. In contrast, LS pooling computes the mean and standard deviation inside a short sliding window (![][image453] frames ![][image454]) around each frame ![][image93], outputting a sequence of length ![][image86] (![][image455])1. Appending ![][image456] to ![][image82] inside MLASP (![][image457]) gives the attention network local syllable-level distribution context around frame ![][image93], yielding a ![][image458] relative EER gain (![][image226] vs. ![][image228])1. |
| **Q4** | In MLASP, the attention network takes ![][image250] as input, but the weighted mean and std are computed over ![][image83]. How are dimensions reconciled? | The attention scoring module uses a two-layer ![][image231] convolutional bottleneck: the first Conv1d maps ![][image459] (followed by ![][image460] and BatchNorm), and the second Conv1d projects ![][image461] before applying softmax over the time axis ![][image86]1. This reduces the attention weight tensor ![][image462] back to the exact dimension of ![][image82] for element-wise multiplication1. |
| **Q5** | Why does AAMSoftmax add an angular margin ![][image379] inside ![][image463] instead of subtracting ![][image379] from ![][image464] (as in CosFace / AM-Softmax)? | On the unit hypersphere, geodesic distance between normalized embeddings equals the angle ![][image465]. Adding ![][image379] directly to ![][image466] enforces a uniform geodesic angular margin across the entire hypersphere, whereas subtracting ![][image379] in cosine space (![][image467]) produces a non-uniform angular penalty that varies nonlinearly with ![][image468]3. |
| **Q6** | Did you identify any mathematical errors or typos in the published paper? | Yes. In Appendix A Equation (3), the denominator of AAMSoftmax is written with the summation index ![][image469]1. Because ![][image38] indexes the sample in the mini-batch and ![][image239] indexes the speaker class, writing ![][image240] is an index-variable error; the mathematically correct condition is ![][image243], where ![][image470] is the ground-truth class label of sample ![][image122]3. |
| **Q7** | Why does IAAMSoftmax (AdaptiveDrop) perform label correction *before* sample filtering, and why does it wait for a warm-up period (ESD \= 5, ESC \= 7)? | During epochs 1–5, network weights and class prototypes ![][image143] are randomly initialized, so cosine similarities are near zero for all samples. Early gradient updates are dominated by coherent clean samples, aligning prototypes ![][image143] with true speaker modes before noise memorization begins (around epoch 15–20)3. Once prototypes are reliable, correcting suspicious labels first rescues mislabeled samples whose true speaker is another training class (preventing over-cleaning), while the subsequent ![][image471] filter acts as a second safety gate to reject uncorrected outliers1. |
| **Q8** | Where does the threshold ![][image5] come from? | ![][image472]1. Under AAMSoftmax (![][image326]), clean intra-class embeddings converge within a cone of ![][image473] around their class center ![][image474], whereas mislabeled impostor samples remain nearly orthogonal (![][image475], ![][image476]) prior to memorization. Thus, ![][image6] (![][image5]) cleanly separates hard positives from mislabeled outliers1. |
| **Q9** | Why does IAAMSoftmax improve EER over AAMSoftmax by only ![][image282] in Table IV (![][image12]), but by ![][image477] (![][image25]) in Table VI? | Table IV is fully supervised training on VoxCeleb2 dev, where speaker labels are already ![][image478] clean, leaving minimal label noise for AdaptiveDrop to filter1. Table VI is self-supervised training on pseudo-labels generated by clustering 1.09M utterances into 5,994 clusters via CAMSAT1. Unsupervised clustering inevitably introduces ![][image479] label noise via cluster merges and splits, which is the exact regime where AdaptiveDrop prevents noise memorization1. |
| **Q10** | Why does your implementation achieve ![][image313] EER on LibriSpeech test-clean whereas the paper reports ![][image16] EER on VoxCeleb1-O? | Two quantitative scaling factors explain the gap: (1) VoxCeleb2 dev has ![][image480] training speakers (1.09M utterances)1, whereas LibriSpeech train-clean-100 has ![][image481] speakers (28.5k utterances)—a ![][image314] difference in speaker count. Published LibriSpeech ASV scaling studies20 prove ![][image482], predicting ![][image483] EER at 251 speakers. (2) We scaled channels ![][image321] and ![][image322] (![][image444] params) to fit student GPU memory and prevent overfitting. Crucially, all relative ablation trends from Table II and Table VI hold. |
| **Q11** | Why was it critical to enforce *different chapter IDs* when generating target trials on LibriSpeech? | In LibriSpeech, all utterances within a single \<chapter\_id\> were recorded in one sitting with identical microphone distance and room acoustics. Pairing utterances from the same chapter allows a CNN to achieve ![][image327] EER simply by matching background room tone and channel coloration. Enforcing cross-chapter target pairs forces true biometric speaker verification across recording sessions. |
| **Q12** | Why is cosine similarity used at test time instead of a trained PLDA backend? | As cited in Section II-D of the paper (Refs \[40\]–\[42\])1, when an embedding network is trained with a large-margin angular loss like AAMSoftmax, the loss directly optimizes cosine similarity on the unit hypersphere. Intra-class covariance is already compact and spherical on the hypersphere, making cosine similarity outperform Gaussian PLDA without requiring separate backend training1. |
| **Q13** | What is the difference between EER and minDCF, and why do we report both? | EER evaluates the symmetric operating point where ![][image484], implicitly assuming equal error costs and equal target/impostor priors18. In high-security access control, false acceptances are far more costly than false rejections and genuine target trials may have low prior probability (![][image391])19. minDCF weights ![][image485] by ![][image486] and ![][image487] by ![][image488], measuring reliability in the low-FAR tail of the DET curve17. |
| **Q14** | Where is the parameter bottleneck in the paper's 30.91M-parameter SKA-HNN, and how would you optimize it for production? | Flattening ![][image489] into ![][image490] and concatenating its local statistics (![][image491]) produces a ![][image273] tensor1. The subsequent Conv1d(7680, 512, k=3) layer consumes **11.80M parameters**, and the MLASP bottleneck over ![][image492] channels consumes **8.81M parameters**. Inserting a ![][image231] bottleneck projection compressing ![][image80] from ![][image493] before local statistics and MLFC cuts over **17M parameters** (\>55% of model size) with minimal accuracy loss. |
| **Q15** | Why did you choose LibriSpeech over LibriTTS for this implementation? | First, LibriSpeech is natively sampled at 16 kHz, matching the paper's 80-dim Mel-filterbank setup (25 ms window, 10 ms hop)1, whereas LibriTTS is 24 kHz14. Second, LibriTTS strips internal pauses and discards noisy/expressive segments for TTS synthesis, reducing train-clean-100 from 100.6h to 53.8h and removing natural intra-speaker prosodic variation. Third, LibriSpeech has established ASV benchmarks via the VoicePrivacy Challenge14. |

### **11.3 Honest Project Limitations to State Proactively**

**\[Engineering Recommendation\]** Proactively stating three architectural and experimental limitations during the viva demonstrates mature engineering judgment. First, **Read Audiobook Domain vs. Spontaneous In-the-Wild Speech**: LibriSpeech consists of read English audiobooks (train-clean-100), which exhibit lower emotional variance, fewer overlapping speakers, and cleaner recording conditions than the YouTube celebrity interviews in VoxCeleb24; we mitigate this by evaluating on test-other, injecting synthetic babble and RIR reverberation, and running a zero-shot cross-corpus evaluation on VoxCeleb1-O (Tier 4). Second, **Stand-In Clustering vs. Full I-Vector \+ CAMSAT Pipeline**: replacing the legacy Kaldi 400-dim i-vector \+ CAMSAT deep mutual-information clustering pipeline1 with K-Means/Agglomerative clustering on acoustic/bootstrap features alongside controlled synthetic label noise (![][image13]) isolates the exact same algorithmic property (IAAMSoftmax vs. AAMSoftmax under label noise) while avoiding a multi-week Kaldi GMM-UBM diversion. Third, **Parameter-Count Confounding in Table II**: just as in the original paper's Table II1, removing MLFC (![][image279]) or the 2D-CNN front-end (![][image22]) reduces total trainable parameters alongside structural removal; we explicitly report both parameter counts and EER in our tables so examiners can see the accuracy-per-parameter tradeoff.

## **12\. Appendices**

### **12.1 Glossary of Technical Terms**

| Acronym / Term | Full Technical Name | Concise Engineering Definition |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **AAMSoftmax** | Additive Angular Margin Softmax (ArcFace) | Classification loss that normalizes weights and embeddings to the unit hypersphere and adds an angular margin penalty ![][image379] to the target class angle ![][image494]1. |
| **AdaptiveDrop** | Adaptive Label-Noise Cleansing Scheme | Online training filter that rectifies suspicious labels (epoch \> ESC) and drops samples whose cosine similarity to their class prototype is below ![][image145] (epoch \> ESD)1. |
| **AS-Norm** | Adaptive Symmetric Score Normalization | Post-processing calibration that normalizes a raw cosine score using the mean and standard deviation of the top\-![][image415] highest scores against an unlabeled cohort9. |
| **ASP** | Attentive Statistics Pooling | Temporal aggregation layer that learns frame- and channel-specific importance weights ![][image495] to compute weighted utterance-level mean and standard deviation1. |
| **CAMSAT** | Augmentation Mix and Self-Augmented Training | Deep mutual-information clustering algorithm used by the authors on 400-dim i-vectors to generate 5,994 unsupervised pseudo-labels on VoxCeleb2 dev1. |
| **cwSKA / fwSKA** | Channel-Wise / Frequency-Wise Selective Kernel Attention | Multi-branch attention blocks that dynamically weight parallel convolutional kernels (![][image40] vs. ![][image41]) along the channel or frequency dimension1. |
| **DET Curve** | Detection Error Tradeoff Curve | Biometric error plot of False Rejection Rate (![][image487]) versus False Acceptance Rate (![][image485]) plotted on normal-deviate (probit) axes18. |
| **EER** | Equal Error Rate | Biometric error metric at the operating threshold ![][image289] where False Acceptance Rate equals False Rejection Rate (![][image484])13. |
| **IAAMSoftmax** | Improved Additive Angular Margin Softmax | The paper's combined objective integrating AAMSoftmax (![][image326]) with AdaptiveDrop (![][image5], ESD=5, ESC=7)1. |
| **minDCF** | Minimum Detection Cost Function | NIST SRE weighted detection cost ![][image496] normalized by the default prior cost17. |
| **MLASP & MLFC** | Multi-Level Attentive Statistics Pooling & Feature Combination | Concatenation of multi-stage features ![][image345] augmented with local sliding-window statistics ![][image456] prior to attentive statistics pooling1. |

### **12.3 Command Cheat-Sheet (Setup, Download, Training, Evaluation, Demo)**

Bash  
\# 1\. Environment Setup (Colab or Mac M3 Pro)  
python3 \-m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate  
pip install \--upgrade pip  
pip install torch torchvision torchaudio soundfile librosa scipy scikit-learn \\  
            umap-learn omegaconf tensorboard gradio speechbrain tqdm matplotlib seaborn

\# 2\. Download & Extract LibriSpeech Partitions \+ RIRS\_NOISES (\~7.9 GB total)  
mkdir \-p data/raw && cd data/raw  
wget \-c https\://www\.openslr.org/resources/12/train-clean-100.tar.gz  
wget \-c https\://www\.openslr.org/resources/12/dev-clean.tar.gz  
wget \-c https\://www\.openslr.org/resources/12/test-clean.tar.gz  
wget \-c https\://www\.openslr.org/resources/12/test-other.tar.gz  
wget \-c https\://www\.openslr.org/resources/28/rirs\_noises.zip  
for f in \*.tar.gz; do tar \-xzf "\$f"; done  
unzip \-q rirs\_noises.zip  
cd ../..

\# 3\. Build Manifests, Verify Speaker Disjointness, and Generate Trial Lists  
python scripts/prep\_librispeech.py \--data\_root data/raw/LibriSpeech \--out\_dir data/manifests  
pytest tests/test\_shapes.py tests/test\_metrics.py

\# 4\. Run Tier 0 Baseline (ECAPA-TDNN) & Tier 1 Core (SKA-HNN S0 & S1)  
python scripts/train.py \--config configs/tier0\_ecapa.yaml  
python scripts/train.py \--config configs/tier1\_ska\_hnn.yaml \--loss iaam\_softmax \--exp\_name s0\_iaam  
python scripts/train.py \--config configs/tier1\_ska\_hnn.yaml \--loss aam\_softmax  \--exp\_name s1\_aam

\# 5\. Run Tier 2 Ablations (S2, S3, S5, S6) & Tier 3 Label Noise / SSL Sweep  
python scripts/run\_ablations.py \--config configs/tier2\_ablations.yaml \--systems S2 S3 S5 S6  
python scripts/run\_ssl\_noise.py \--config configs/tier3\_noisy\_ssl.yaml \--noise\_rates 0.1 0.2 0.4 \--run\_kmeans

\# 6\. Evaluate Checkpoints (EER, minDCF, 95% Bootstrap CI, DET, Short-Utterance 1s/2s/3s)  
python scripts/evaluate.py \--ckpt checkpoints/s0\_iaam/best\_eer.pt \\  
    \--trials data/manifests/trials\_test\_clean.txt data/manifests/trials\_test\_other\_hard.txt \\  
    \--as\_norm \--plot\_dir outputs/plots\_s0

\# 7\. Launch Interactive 5-Tab Gradio Demo (Local M3 Pro or Colab Share)  
python app/gradio\_demo.py \--ckpt checkpoints/s0\_iaam/best\_eer.pt \--port 7860
